note_en: The pattern 跟 A (不)一样 "(not) the same as A" runs through this whole text: 这跟爸妈那种每天准时上下班的方式完全不一样 "this is completely different from my parents' clock-in, clock-out routine." English switches between "the same as," "different from" and "unlike," but Chinese keeps one frame and just adds 不 or a degree adverb (不太, 完全, 很) in front of 一样. Note that the adverb goes before 一样, never before 跟.
